column1: # Original PowerPC instruction evidence. Addresses are DOL virtual addresses
# or REL text offsets as interpreted by the calling test. Existing source
# hashes and semantic assertions remain in the tests.
# All supported direct model consumers call that same resolver.
# Enemy source forwards its model through float slot+794, then resolves
# it in the first-frame callback. Key24 is exactly representable.
# Ordinary, scene and interaction paths set actor+9b bits2..5.
# Property dispatch establishes each bit's meaning independently.
# add item ID to save base
# setter uses the same byte index
# The two scenery refresh readers walk the same table and query its
# first flag; they do not supply a separate dynamic flag namespace.
# Constructor installs the same callback checked by each property case.
# Recipe is the sixth constructor operand, stored in its own field.
# Renderer dispatches the signed recipe through its original table.
# Opcode 0C and its transfer of the flag word to the initializer.
# Store flags, test bit 1, initialize timer to 300 or 1.
# Message-end persistent/autopage and active-choice paths precede timer.
# Decrement, and request close only at zero.
# Renderer: Green, Red, then bit 512, before the default tint.
# r13 is initialized to 80362000; -8000 selects color at 8035A000.
# Query loads type/key, sign-extends type, then compares record status/key.
# Touch circle: record index * 52, status = 1 at global+2f70.
# Confirmed circle and triangle: status = 3, independent of shape byte.
# Both handlers forward their first operand as the formation request,
# followed by arena and defeat policy, to the shared setup helper.
# Enemy call: second script argument -> r31 -> setup's third argument.
# Simple call: second and third arguments -> arena and defeat policy.
# Long call: same arena/policy positions; fourth argument is music.
# Shared setup: arena at request+8; insert only r5 bit0 into byte bit3.
# Completion: defeat==3, other override clear, request bit3 clear
# selects mode12/game over. An odd policy suppresses that transition.
# Long handler: music 0 becomes -1; store signed halfword at +0x10.
# Battle loader reads signed halfword. -1 selects its automatic themes;
# every other value goes directly to the music-play wrapper.
# Mode9/battle branch has a distinct protocol. Its non--1 resource
# selectors, including zero, go directly through resource resolution.
# Field selector0: disable scripted animation, clear its pointer, and
# take only the duration operand. Both branches join at 8004C998,
# skipping the model index lookup and the flags load/store.
# Only selector -1 reads the third operand at args+238. It is a
# byte offset into object+C0's table, with a fallback at offset12.
# Every other nonzero selector resolves the resource pointer itself.
# flags are read only in the nonzero branch
# shared object callback after both branches
# Simple call sign-extends its first operand and forwards the public
# cue to the common sound service; the service uses its u16 encoding.
# Both branches of the extended call reach that same cue namespace.
# Extended call pops binding, volume, pan offset, cue, in that order.
# Signed pan_offset /2 rounded toward zero, +64; out of range resets64.
# Volume255 reads the field level. Binding255 selects unbound playback.
# A bound cue-1 clears the three halfwords at802C8E90+index*6.
# Simple call uses the same pan conversion and the current field level.
# Common services apply pan and volume separately after voice creation.
# Only operation100 applies a field-default volume. Stop102 and
# unknown operations (including255) do not enter this branch.
# Slot volume narrows to a byte before the common volume service.
# Spatial services retain all eight bits during distance attenuation.
# Volume becomes controller7 with the value unchanged.
# Both MIDI and FX controller stores keep seven bits, without clamping.
# Ambient handler pops radius, byte volume, full-width cue, then actor.
# Mode9 has no actor, regardless of the cue; the shared join skips stores.
# F423F/999999 resolves directly to the controlled actor at 802C7EA0.
# Only full-width -1 takes the disable branch. 65535 still enables it.
# Ambient update uses the byte volume and float radius, and forwards
# the retained cue's u16 bits to the common field sound service.
# Its volume byte 255 selects the current field sound-level byte.
# One-shot actor audio uses the same radius/volume/cue order and mode9
# guard, but forwards a signed-halfword cue and unbound slot 255.
# Direct-velocity constructor: factory args, object fields and narrowing.
# Normalized-direction constructor: separate speed divided by100 before float conversion.
# Factory bounds/palette/dispatch; falling/rising leaf callbacks; texture-slot callback selection.
# Script-local name query: arguments, literal battle key, field aliases, name source and signed result.
# Fixed body-part query: arguments, literal battle key, field aliases, name source and signed result.
# Fixed rotation: slots/bones, skip, host/key lookup and component/interpolation inputs.
# Timed rotation: slots/bones, skip, host/key lookup and component/interpolation inputs.
# Percentage scale: slots/bones, skip, host/key lookup and component/interpolation inputs.
# Translation: slot/bone stack slots, -1 no-op before lookup, raw battle key request
# Field actor lookup includes controlled/scenery aliases
# Translation helper call: zero interpolation denominator becomes one
# Wait producer stores actor key, wait kind20 and float target frame
# Translation helper uses controller stride74, bone index and XYZ target/delta records
# Wait consumer: battle requests compare exact frame and release missing actors
# Wait consumer resolves the controlled alias each poll
# Field missing actor stays pending; integer frame equality clears the wait
# Stereo toggle and native sound-mode update
# Every clear increments the old count, capped100, and refunds the first selected benefit
# Count query, leader lock, title/game-over transitions, menu toggle, credits
# New Game Plus snapshots saved state and carry flags
# Return the old result and discard two arguments
# Automatic line: status/shape, full-width key and ordered coordinate/height halfword stores.
# Touch line: status/shape, full-width key and ordered coordinate/height halfword stores.
# Confirmed line: status/shape, full-width key and ordered coordinate/height halfword stores.
# Touch triangle: status/shape, full-width key and ordered coordinate/height halfword stores.
# Automatic remover: type/key comparison, clear record, repeat until no match.
# Touch remover: type/key comparison, clear record, repeat until no match.
# Confirmed remover: type/key comparison, clear record, repeat until no match.
# Contact consumer: signed Z endpoints plus height, then XY endpoints to circle/segment intersection.
# Constructor: six arguments, numbered and actor-key aliases, base/array tracks, resource resolver, frame/rate/flags stores.
# Clear: only2/3 leave the main-bank path; base and array tracks are reset.
# Seek: only2/3 leave the main-bank path; frame clamp and store.
# Rate: same numbered-only routing, signed input divided by200 in
# native animation-frame units and stored at+18.
# both field branches store its low byte
# Scene actor: key, XYZ/heading, model and behavior/speed stack slots.
# Interaction actor: key, XYZ/heading, model and behavior/speed stack slots.
# Ordinary spawn loads its eight arguments before the mode9 branch.
# Battle request is [key, resource kind, model pointer]. Kinds17..19
# bypass field-model resolution. No field behavior or speed is forwarded.
# Only the nonbattle path tests the controlled-player key and emote range.
# Collision and scenery constructors retain the literal signed key,
# bind a model and store their own behavior byte/speed, without emotes.
# allocator overwrites incoming r3, not a script reader
# Shared initializer: flags=1 at +1c, completion bits=0 at +20.
# Field configuration stores its u16 flags, initializes a track, then
# ORs those flags into the initializer's default value.
# Field update0 only clears pause bit2. Update2 ORs it, while other
# nonzero updates replace the lower halfword and retain upper flags.
# Shared reader's two inlined advancement paths test Paused (2),
# Once (8), and internal high flags. Bit0 is not the loop switch.
# Battle configuration stores its signed-byte flags in the same track.
# Battle update0 also only clears bit2. All nonzero updates replace
# the lower flags, including update2 (unlike the field special case).
# All three battle-entry APIs suspend with wait command 23.
# Original wait dispatcher and table entry for command 23.
# Once battle mode ends, copy battle-state status to shared word 0x24.
# Dialogue completion can write the same word: it is not permanently typed.
